Graphs built once per input shape

Source: R/state.R
zl_graph_cache.Rd

zl_graph_cache() wraps zl_graph() for loops whose input shapes vary, such as a decoder whose count of new positions changes. Its graphs are built by zl_forward() the first time it sees a set of input shapes, and reused after. An input given as an R integer vector or array becomes an integer input (see zl_int()); any other numeric input is f32.

Usage

zl_graph_cache(build, p, loss = NULL, outputs = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'zl_graph_cache'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

build

A function of one argument, the named list of inputs, returning a tensor or a named list of tensors.

p

The parameter store whose parameters build() uses.

loss

The name of a scalar output to train on (see the training functions); NULL for none.

outputs

The names of the outputs to keep, of those build() returns; NULL for all.

x

A graph cache.

...

Unused.

Value

A graph cache, of class zl_graph_cache, for zl_forward(). length() gives the number of graphs it holds.

Details

When the store's and the cached graphs' memory together would pass getOption("zulm.max_bytes"), the graphs used least recently are freed first; the graph just built is kept.

Examples

p <- zl_params()
zl_param(p, "w", c(3, 2))
gc <- zl_graph_cache(function(x) zl_crossprod(zl_param_tensor(p, "w"), x$input), p)
dim(zl_forward(gc, list(input = matrix(1, 3, 5)))$output)
#> [1] 2 5
dim(zl_forward(gc, list(input = matrix(1, 3, 7)))$output)
#> [1] 2 7
length(gc)
#> [1] 2
